people.gloss: The blood of resentment turns to jade (Lý Hạ: hận huyết thiên niên thổ trung bích)
people.role: Founder and head of Thu Phần Các (960): soul arts and grave wards among the graves of Lôi Trạch Thành (ma đạo)
people.appearance: A gaunt woman in undyed hemp mourning, with grave-earth in the hem and a small bronze bell at her wrist that rings when no one moves.
people.backstory: Lý Hận Bích was born in 830 among the cave hunters of Thủ Động Trại, high on the thunder ridge, where Khải Lôi once kept wardens over the cave in which it laid the disciples its storm climbs killed (A283, V152). Every Kinh Trập the hunters went in to sweep the dead and came out before the first thunder. At twelve she was too slow, and the door was barred behind her by the hunters' own rule. She spent the night among Khải Lôi's dead. Darkness formed in her root, and she heard them sing. She left the ridge at forty and learned soul arts and grave wards from whoever would teach a ma đạo girl. In 960 she came down to the graves of Lôi Trạch Thành, Khải Lôi's city, burned by its own head's tribulation in 480 (C053, C008). No dead on the continent had more cause, and they sang the loudest. She founded the Pavilion on the bamboo hill above them and swore it to the Tower (C197). Since then the villagers of Ương Ca have sung louder at planting to drown the graves out (A314). In 1110 her sworn sister Lương Thanh Mộ (luong_thanh_mo) went into the deepest grave and did not come back. Lý hears her voice among the singers every autumn.
people.wants: To hear the oldest song of Lôi Trạch to its end before it is drunk dry, and to see a whole stone of grave jade ripen in her lifetime, not a fleck.
people.secret: The oldest graves do not sing poems. They sing what their head was chanting when his tribulation burned the city: passages of Khải Lôi's own canon. Cơ Ký Âm has written them down. She has sealed his copybooks and told the Tower nothing. And she has the river's drowned and the hamlet's unclaimed dead laid in the jade beds to be sung, though the abbess of Cốc Vũ pays rice every autumn for them to lie at the edge; the rice buys her censers.

people.role: Singing master of the Pavilion, who leads the autumn chant at the graves
people.appearance: A soft-spoken old man with a zither on his back and a voice that can fill a valley without being raised.
people.backstory: A drum-maker's son from the ruins of Kích Cổ Đường, where the last drummers scattered in 482 (V153). He heard the graves of Lôi Trạch sing at ten, seventeen tiles off, and walked to them. Lương Thanh Mộ (luong_thanh_mo) taught him the songs, and after she went into the deepest grave in 1110 Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich) finished his training. Every autumn he leads the chant and listens for one voice, and he sings her grave last and lightly. He also takes the rice Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu) pays for the river's drowned, writes back that they lie at the edge, and lays them in the jade beds as the head orders.

people.appearance: A square-shouldered woman with a jade-cutter's lens on a cord and dirt to the elbows.
people.backstory: Born on the Pavilion's hill to a grave-digger and raised by the sect. Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich) made her keeper of the jade beds. In a hundred years the beds gave her three green flecks, and she thinks the head too patient. For three autumns Tiết Ấn Sương (tiet_an_suong) laid a forcing seal over one of the oldest graves by the river, and Thẩm sang it dry inside the chant; it gave out on the last night of last autumn, after the singers had gone up. At midsummer she dug a ripe stone out of it. Kiều Mãn Lâu's (kieu_man_lau) man is carrying it to Thu Trì in a fish basket, ten weeks on the road, for the pills that would make her Kết Đan.

people.role: Copyist of the songs of the graves; he has written down what the oldest dead sing
people.appearance: A thin, short-sighted man who writes with his left hand and holds his right over his ear, as if shading it from a wind.
people.backstory: Cơ Ký Âm was born in 1130 in Không Mông Thành, the valley city that Lôi Trạch's survivors moved up to a year after the tribulation burned their own (A285). His family have been copyists for six hundred years, and his grandmother told him their people came from the graves. He walked down to the Pavilion at twenty with a good ear and a box of brushes, and Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich) set him to write down the songs. For fifty autumns he has knelt at the graves and taken them down word by word. The new graves sing poems. The oldest, by the river where the lightning first struck, sing something else, in a cadence like a drum. In 1190 he understood it: the dead are chanting what their head chanted as his tribulation came down, the canon of Khải Lôi Môn (C008, C035). He showed the head. She sealed his copybooks in the ward and told him to tell no one. The Tower's vault master Lệ Tiêu Hồn (le_tieu_hon) has since asked twice to borrow a book of autumn songs.
people.wants: To finish the oldest song, and to have the dead's words read by someone who will not burn them.
people.secret: He kept a second copy of the drum passages, sewn into the lining of his winter robe, and he has played their cadence once on a grave drum. Something under the ridge answered.

people.role: The cave hunters' son: keeps the Pavilion's Cave Hall at Thủ Động Trại, one of its two dark singers
people.appearance: A short, heavy hunter in ridge furs with a cave lamp on his belt that he never lights.
people.backstory: Born in the hunters' village at Thủ Động Trại, the head's own, five generations down from her sister. On his own Kinh Trập night in the cave the Darkness the ridge gave him woke. Since 1185 he has kept the Pavilion's Cave Hall there (V152). Each Kinh Trập he shuts the likeliest hunters' child in the cave of Khải Lôi's dead by the hunters' own rule, as Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich) was shut in at twelve, and sends the ones who come out with nothing home with a fee for the family. He and Chử Ẩn Thạch (chu_an_thach) sing the cave's dead as the river singers sing the graves.

people.role: First elder of Thu Phần Các and the head's sworn sister; one of the voices in the graves
people.backstory: Born in the hamlet that grew on the ruins of Lôi Trạch, she was the first to answer when Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich) came to the graves in 960. She taught the songs to Bào Thu Xướng (bao_thu_xuong) and laid the wards beside the head for a hundred and fifty years. In 1110 the oldest ward by the river began to fail, and she went down into the grave to renew it from inside (N-thu_phan-02). The ward held. Every autumn since, the Pavilion hears a new voice in the chorus.
